title: Shelves, stock and shop upgrades
summary: Your shop grows by buying better furniture and upgrades: TCG Card Shop Simulator separates shelf types, shop items and upgrade kinds, so each purchase changes what you can sell and how much fits.
body: Shelves are not all the same: there are plain shelves, card shelves and combination shelves that hold both cards and items.
A shelf manager keeps track of what is on your shelves, which is why restocking is a task rather than an automatic process.
Shop purchases are grouped into defined kinds, and upgrades are a separate set of choices.

The stock the shop offers is data as well. It keeps every item type it shows along with a list of items, a list of the meshes those items are drawn as and a list of the quest sequence it prefers to present them in, which is why the catalogue can be ordered rather than shuffled.
What this entry does not tell you: prices of furniture, upgrade costs or how much space each shelf has. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: There are several shelf kinds, including one for cards and one that combines cards and items.
Shelf contents are tracked by a manager.
Shop purchases are grouped into fixed kinds.
Upgrades are a separate, defined set.
The stock item data holds every item type it shows along with an item list, a mesh list and a list of the quest sequence it prefers.
